Jerome H. Powell: Given the emerging risks to the U.S. economy and inflation running below our 2% target, the Committee should begin lowering the federal funds rate at its next meeting to support continued economic growth and achieve our inflation goals. Proactive rate cuts are appropriate to address these challenges and sustain favorable labor market conditions.

Given the current economic conditions and inflation below target, it is appropriate for the Committee to begin easing policy now to support the economy. Waiting for more data risks allowing downside risks to materialize and weaken the outlook further.

Given the current inflation below target and rising risks to the economy, it is appropriate and urgent to reduce the level of policy restriction to support growth and employment. We have already begun easing monetary policy and stand ready to take further action as needed.

Given the current inflation below target and a moderate unemployment rate, I would support a 25 basis point cut at the coming meeting to sustain economic growth and address emerging risks. This adjustment aligns with our objective to foster maximum employment and price stability.

Yes, the time has come to dial back policy restraint to support the economy amid evolving risks. We will take appropriate steps to move toward a more accommodative stance to foster maximum employment and price stability.

This will support the economy while maintaining control over the federal funds rate through appropriate tools.

Given that inflation remains below target and labor market slack persists, it is appropriate to maintain the current accommodative policy stance and wait for more data before considering easing. Premature easing could undermine progress toward our inflation and employment goals.

Given the modest inflation below target and rising fiscal support, it is urgent to reduce policy restraint to sustain economic growth and prevent a downturn. Maintaining current rates risks unnecessarily slowing the economy amid improving fiscal conditions.

Given the current economic conditions with inflation below target and rising uncertainties, I support a 25 basis point cut at the coming meeting to provide additional accommodation and support economic growth. This adjustment aligns with our mandate to foster maximum employment and price stability.

Yes, the time has come to dial back policy restraint as the diminishing fiscal restraint and accommodative monetary policy support continued economic growth. We should carefully adjust to sustain expansion while monitoring inflation and labor market conditions.

Bowman: Given inflation is below target and the labor market remains relatively strong, the Committee should consider lowering the federal funds rate at its next meeting to support economic growth and help move inflation toward our 2% goal. Given inflation remains below target and the labor market is still relatively strong, it is premature to start easing policy now; the Committee should wait for more data to assess the economic impact of recent developments before adjusting. Given the current inflation below target and a moderate unemployment rate, it is not urgent to reduce the current level of policy restriction. Maintaining a cautious stance allows us to support continued economic growth while monitoring inflation dynamics.
